title: Adopting AI in pharma and biotech, producing  decisions worth making 💊
description:
In pharma and biotech, adopting AI is no longer the question. Whether it produces decisions worth making is. 💊

The binding constraint is context.

An LLM without context generates plausible text. It does not generate warranted decisions.

Two conditions close that gap:

The business context of each use case (data, actors, regulatory and operational constraints) is explicit and computable
That context can evolve without breaking the system
MetaDot is a methodology built to meet both. Not a product, but a disciplined approach to combining knowledge graphs and LLM-based AI to build use-case-specific semantic layers within a strictly defined scope. It integrates four elements: people and skills, processes, data, and technology.

Two properties set it apart:

A meta-layer that semi-automatically constructs the semantic layer each use case requires, instead of delivering monolithic and rigid semantic solutions
Learning across use cases at operational, tactical and strategic levels, so AI-generated outcomes stay coherent across functions and organisational levels
Business value is built in. It is defined at the outset, measured during execution and monitored after delivery.

The approach has been implemented and tested at different scales, in several organisations, across Research, Clinical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, Safety and Pharmacovigilance, Real-World Evidence and Market Access.

🎤 Cedric Berger, Head of Knowledge Management, MIGx
